classification.difficultyReason: Find the upper rectangle's width from its area, interpret the labelled extension to obtain the lower rectangle's full width, then use its area to calculate x.

spec.description: An upper-left rectangle sits on a wider lower rectangle, with aligned left edges and the shared horizontal boundary retained.
spec.mathematics: The upper rectangle has area 25.2 cm² and height 3 cm. The lower rectangle has area 195 cm² and height x. The 11.1 cm dimension spans only the width beyond the upper rectangle's right edge.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied areas, supplied dimensions and the unknown label are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $w$ be the upper rectangle's width and $l$ the lower rectangle's width.
Use $A=\text{length}\times\text{width}$ for each rectangle.
$$\begin{align*}25.2&=3w\\w&=\frac{25.2}{3}\\w&=8.4\text{ cm}\\l&=8.4+11.1\\l&=19.5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
For the lower rectangle:
$$\begin{align*}195&=19.5x\\x&=\frac{195}{19.5}\\x&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
